PullRequest.Title: agentHost: reduce artifact tool overhead with a prompt experiment
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- Add the experiment-configurable `chat.artifactTools.compactPrompts` setting, defaulting to **false** (verbose/control). The treatment key is `config.chat.artifactTools.compactPrompts`. Compact prompts reduce repeated classification prose and first-turn guidance while retaining the full eligibility contract in the Add tool description for restored chats.
- Keep List/Remove deferral **independent of the prompt experiment**. Typed per-tool metadata keeps Add eager, uses Copilot discovery when its existing search gate is active, and uses Claude's native MCP loading metadata. Codex stays eager because the host cannot reliably determine native search support.
- Make Add idempotently promote references in place, preserve IDs and atomic batches, and return concise per-item mutation results. Preserve actual tool names, legacy aliases, feature gating, explicit removal, and user-visible labels. The existing authoritative PR-creation registration path remains unchanged.

## Experiment and measurement

Start a new chat after changing the prompt setting. Both variants use the same deferral behavior and shared eligibility/discovery clarifications; the control retains the original verbose format rather than reproducing the old payload byte-for-byte.

Local `o200k_base` measurements of serialized tool-definition arrays plus the first-turn reminder, with List/Remove deferred in both variants:

| Artifact-specific payload | Control | Compact |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Initial tool definitions | 568 | 500 |
| First-turn reminder | 218 | 46 |
| Total | 786 | 546 |

This is **240 fewer initial artifact-specific tokens** from prompt compaction. The eager fallback also saves 240 tokens (888 to 648). Measurements exclude provider framing and later discovery overhead and do **not** establish total-session cost or AIU savings.

## Validation

- 83 targeted Electron tests and 8 Node checks passed, including native Claude SDK/MCP invocation.
- Coverage includes experiment defaults/overrides and host sync, both prompt variants, discovery and invocation, restored/legacy compatibility, gate off/on, first-turn reminders, multi-item adds, duplicate/promotion behavior, atomic failures, URI validation, persistence, and removal.
- `npm run typecheck-client`, changed-file ESLint, `npm run gulp compile-client`, `npm run precommit` (23 staged files), and `git diff --check` passed.
- Full Copilot E2E replay could not complete: the standalone agent host timed out during startup before the scenario ran. No replay recordings were changed; the existing batch-result assertion was updated for the compact success response.

Scenarios.Scenario: Starting or restoring an agent chat with artifact tools enabled across Copilot, Claude, and Codex
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Tool definitions are selected once while constructing the provider session. Copilot and Claude mark List/Remove deferred when provider search is available; Codex keeps all three eager. Provider session startup remains the critical path, but the diff reduces eager definition payload for supported providers and does not add a new blocking operation.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provider session/model startup receives serialized tool definitions.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider startup payload per launch/resume; artifact definition cardinality is reduced from three eager tools to one where search is active.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: All server tools were eager in Copilot, and Claude had no artifact-specific alwaysLoad metadata.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing provider startup boundary is on the critical path; the diff reduces its eager prompt payload rather than adding calls.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Codex thread/start serializes dynamicTools to the Codex process.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One IPC request per thread start, carrying the same three artifact tools when enabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same artifact tools were already included eagerly in dynamicTools.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Existing thread startup IPC remains on the critical path; no additional request or fan-out is introduced.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Three artifact tools per enabled session; effective cardinality is fixed, with two deferred and one eager for Copilot/Claude, and all three eager for Codex.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Copilot and Codex map definitions synchronously once per launch/resume. Claude creates the fixed tool set with Promise.all, but SDK module loading is cached and there are only three artifact definitions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Static original/compact definition arrays are allocated once at module load. Configuration is read from in-memory root state when definitions are selected; the Claude SDK module is cached after first load. No miss loop or negative-cache retry is introduced.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: provider construction paths and deferral gates are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact token and provider startup savings depend on provider framing and model support for tool search, but call counts and fixed definition cardinality are established.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Definition selection adds only bounded in-memory reads and supported providers reduce eager serialized prompt content.

Scenarios.Scenario: Sending the first turn in a new chat with artifact guidance enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The contribution performs two in-memory configuration reads and appends exactly one selected instruction before the first model request. Restored non-empty chats and subsequent turns do not repeat the instruction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: The existing first model request includes the selected artifact guidance in its prompt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly once per new chat; zero on later turns and restored chats with history.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The first request already included artifact guidance once; the diff selects compact or original wording.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The instruction is part of the existing model request, not a separate boundary. Compact treatment reduces bytes; control remains bounded to one request.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One instruction per new or empty restored chat, independent of turn count; no per-message growth after the first turn.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous contribution assembly; no queue or parallel work is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A per-chat memento records first-turn completion. Compact/original strings are module-level constants; there is no external cache or repeated construction.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: memento lifecycle and first-turn tests establish the frequency.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider tokenization varies, but the once-per-chat bound is explicit.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The experiment changes bounded prompt bytes without introducing another request or repeated work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Adding a batch of artifacts, including promoting an existing reference
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Inputs are validated in memory, then one per-session sequenced mutation scans the current artifact list for each batch entry. If the final collection changes, one catalog persistence operation completes before state publication and tool completion.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Catalog synchronization persists the final artifact metadata list.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one persistence operation per mutating Add tool call, regardless of batch size; unchanged duplicate batches perform none.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Batched additions already persisted once per changed call. The new promotion case changes a former duplicate no-op into one required persistence operation because authoritative state now changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Persistence is awaited before the Add tool returns and state is published.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Cost is O(batch size × current artifact count), as before for batched additions. Promotion adds one list map for a matching reference. Effective collections are user-visible session artifacts and expected to remain small; persistence is once for the entire batch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: SessionArtifacts uses SequencerByKey, serializing mutations per session while allowing different sessions to proceed independently. No concurrency burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Current artifacts are read from authoritative session metadata for each mutation; unchanged duplicates do not persist. There is no cache miss retry path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: mutation loop, reference equality check, sequencer, and persistence call are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No repository-wide upper bound for artifact count is visible, but the feature guidance defaults to sparse registration and realistic session lists are small.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. Promotion adds bounded CPU/allocation and only the single durable write required by the new state change; batching and per-session serialization are preserved.

Scenarios.Scenario: Listing or removing artifacts after List/Remove are deferred
Scenarios.CriticalPath: With active tool search, the model discovers the deferred List/Remove definition before invoking it. List reads session metadata in process; Remove performs one sequenced catalog persistence operation. Without search support, tools remain eager.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Copilot tool search round-trips through the existing client tool-search mechanism before a deferred List/Remove invocation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one discovery interaction when the model needs either of the two deferred tools; zero when tool search is inactive because they remain eager.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: List and Remove were always eager and could be invoked without discovery.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Discovery can add latency to the uncommon explicit List/Remove workflow, trading it for smaller eager prompts on all chats.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Removing an artifact synchronizes updated session metadata to the catalog.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One persistence operation for a successful removal; zero for a missing id.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Successful removals already performed the same single persistence operation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing durable write remains awaited before tool completion.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Discovery candidates are fixed at two artifact tools. Listing output scales with recorded artifact count; removal scans that list once, both unchanged from before.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Discovery is provider-controlled and bounded to a fixed candidate set. Removal is serialized per session by SequencerByKey; no aggregate burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Provider tool-search state is resolved at launch. Deferred definitions remain available as fixed metadata; there is no repeated host-side discovery miss or unbounded cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the added discovery step and fixed cardinality; lower only for user-frequency magnitude.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The prevalence of explicit List/Remove requests and provider-specific discovery latency is unknown.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added discovery step is a deliberate, bounded scheduling tradeoff for rare management tools, with eager fallback when search is unavailable; evidence does not establish material user impact warranting rollback.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 24 changed files. Traced provider startup, first-turn prompt assembly, tool discovery, artifact mutation, sequencing, and catalog persistence. No high-confidence actionable performance regression was introduced, and no concrete shipped regression fix met the blame/reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
